record.original_question: For k >= 3, estimate Q_k(X), the number up to X of k-highly composite integers of the form 2^alpha_1 3^alpha_2 ... p_k^alpha_k that beat all smaller integers of the same restricted prime-support form in number of divisors. More generally, for k > 2 and the multiplicative function f_k defined by f_k(p^alpha) = alpha + 1 for alpha <= k and f_k(p^alpha) = 0 for alpha > k, determine or sharply estimate the limiting growth of log Q_{f_k}(X) / log X.

evidence.quote: but no estimation for Qk (X) is given for k >= 3
it seems difficult to find a good estimate for lim

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer $k\geq 1$, call a positive integer $n$ a $k$-restricted highly composite number if $n$ has the form $n=2^{\alpha_1}3^{\alpha_2}\cdots p_k^{\alpha_k}$ (where $p_j$ denotes the $j$-th prime), and $d(n)>d(m)$ for every positive integer $m<n$ of the same restricted form $m=2^{\beta_1}3^{\beta_2}\cdots p_k^{\beta_k}$, where $d(\cdot)$ counts divisors. Let $Q_k(X)$ denote the number of $k$-restricted highly composite integers not exceeding $X$.

(a) For $k\geq 3$, obtain an asymptotic estimate (or sharp upper and lower bounds) for $Q_k(X)$ as $X\to\infty$.

More generally, for an integer $k\geq 2$ define the multiplicative function
$$f_k(p^\alpha)=\begin{cases}\alpha+1,& 0\le\alpha\le k,\\ 0,& \alpha>k,\end{cases}$$
and call $n$ an $f_k$-champion if $f_k(n)>f_k(m)$ for all $m<n$. Let $Q_{f_k}(X)$ be the count of $f_k$-champions up to $X$.

(b) For $k>2$, determine the limiting behavior of $\dfrac{\log Q_{f_k}(X)}{\log X}$ as $X\to\infty$, and give a sharp evaluation of this limit if it exists.
artifact.status_search_result: No source establishes an asymptotic for $Q_k(X)$ with $k\ge 3$ or a sharp value of $\lim \log Q_{f_k}(X)/\log X$. Nicolas's classical estimates address the unrestricted highly composite counting function $Q(X)$, with a conjectured limit $\log 30/\log 16$, but the restricted-support variants for $k\ge 3$ appear unresolved in the literature surveyed.

status_evidence.title: Highly composite number - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Nicolas conjectured lim ln(Q(x))/ln ln(x) = ln(30)/ln(16); results address the unrestricted counting function.
status_evidence.claim: Estimates of Q(X) exist for the unrestricted case (Erdős, Nicolas); restricted variants are not covered.

status_evidence.title: Highly Composite Numbers (arXiv:2305.14350)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of highly composite numbers and Q(x) asymptotics.
status_evidence.claim: No asymptotic for the restricted Q_k(X) with k>=3 is given.
